newsitem.title: BELARUS: Thousands in Belarus protest at Russian union plan.
newsitem.headline: Thousands in Belarus protest at Russian union plan.

text.p: About 3,000 people waving nationalist flags and carrying banners reading "Russia means war" protested on Wednesday against plans for a union of Belarus with its giant fellow Slav neighbour.

Semyon Sharetsky, head of the parliament disbanded by hardline President Alexander Lukashenko after a controversial referendum last November, told the rally in the centre of the capital: "No to Slav fascism!"

A period for "people's discussion" on the planned union of 150 million Russians and 10 million Belarussians ends on Thursday and a charter is due to be signed by Lukashenko and Russian President Boris Yeltsin on May 23.

A large section of the population of Russia's small western neighbour support the idea of a union but nationalists actively oppose it, fearing a return to the dominance by Moscow they experienced in Soviet days.
Opinion polls in both countries have shown most people back the idea of closer integration and even a merger.

But some in Russia and Belarus nationalists, who do not trust promises by Yeltsin and Lukashenko that the deal will not affect the sovereignty of either state, accuse Russia of imperialistic plans and see the union as a threat.

Russian liberals, who generally welcome closer integration with Belarus, have warned Yeltsin against striking a deal with the hardline Lukashenko, whose authoritarian rule and crackdown on civil rights have been criticised abroad.
